newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile cuts interbank rate 25 basis points.
newsitem.headline: Chile cuts interbank rate 25 basis points.

text.p: The Chilean Central Bank cut the interbank borrowing rate to 6.75 percent annual from 7.00 percent, the bank said in a statement.
The cut was made possible by the progress against inflation, the bank said. It was the third relaxing of interest rates by the Central Bank this year.

"In consideration of the recent advances in the reduction of inflation and in the evolution of its nearest determining factors, the Council of the Central Bank has deemed it appropriate for the interbank interest rates to stand in a range centered at an equivalent of 6.75 percent annual," said the statement.
"This represents a reduction of 25 basis points with respect to the previous range," it said.
The council will continue to monitor inflation and growth "to ensure fulfillment of the inflation goal for this year and maintain a gradual reduction in inflation next year," said the statement.

Consumer inflation in May stood at a mere 0.2 percent, the government announced Tuesday, a figure which officials said almost guaranteed fulfillment of the Central Bank's annual target of 5.5 to six percent inflation. ((--Froilan Romero/Roger Atwood, Santiago newsroom +56-2-699-5595 x211))
